chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Three-way credit for "Stompin' at the Savoy"
summary: McRae persuaded Sampson to give Goodman a third of the song, so Goodman's Camel show would make it a hit.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So, Benny Goodman was up one night, and he said, That's "Stompin At The Savoy" y'all playing. I like it."
And he had his Camel Show. (Inaudible). "When can you get me a piece of that song?"
At that time --
See, because I was getting music from downtown, all the publishers. I knew everybody down there.
Chick says, "Well" --
So I told him, "I'll talk to Sampson about it and I'll talk to Chick."

The agreement was that I made with Sampson was, I say, "Look, what do you have to lose? Benny Goodman is on the air. Give him a third of the thing."
"He wants to make it a big song. You know he's got all the air time. He got that Camel Show."
He'll "(inaudible) broadcast it for you it'll be a coast to coast and (inaudible) big number. Cut him in on the thing."
So Sampson say, "I'll give you a piece of (inaudible)."
He agreed to give Chick a piece (inaudible). Three way split -- Chick Webb, Benny Goodman, and Edgar Sampson.
And the song became a big song. Benny played it on the Camel Show and became "Stompin At The Savoy."
You know, like I wrote "Back Bay Shuffle" for Artie. Artie come up from "Back Bay" --
It wasn't the idea, it was the idea that he was coming from back bay -- "Here's "Back Bay

Shuffle." You know, he would go in there with this things, you know. It became a big song.
So this is why Benny's got his name on the song. He agreed, said okay. Benny agreed to do it.
And then we give him the arrangement. Sampson made an arrangement on it for his band. And that was it.
That was the big song!
Then that moved Sampson up. Then we began to play the rest of --
Then Benny began to play the rest of Sampson's thing like "Blue Lou," and all that other stuff that Sampson wrote, you know. "Don't Be That Way," you know.
And out of that, he took all the other (inaudible). He say, "What else you got?"
And he didn't get his name on those songs. Benny just said give him piece of "Stompin At The Savoy." He started making all the other things big.
